genesis.29.p1.b1.text: Jacob resumed his journey and came to the land of the people of the east. He looked and saw a well in the field, and near it lay three flocks of sheep, …

genesis.29.p1.b2.text: … because the sheep were watered from this well. And a large stone covered the mouth of the well.

genesis.29.p1.b3.text: When all the flocks had been gathered there, the shepherds would roll away the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep. Then they would return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well.

genesis.29.p2.b2.text: “Do you know Laban the grandson of Nahor?”

genesis.29.p2.b3.text: “Yes,” … “and here comes his daughter Rachel with his sheep.”

genesis.29.p2.b4.text: “Look,” … “it is still broad daylight; it is not yet time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep and take them back to pasture.”

genesis.29.p2.b5.text: “We cannot, until all the flocks have been gathered … Then we will water the sheep.”

genesis.29.p3.b1.text: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

genesis.29.p3.b2.text: As soon as Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother’s brother Laban, with Laban’s sheep, …

genesis.29.p3.b3.text: … he went up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle’s sheep.

genesis.29.p4.b3.text: He told Rachel that he was Rebekah’s son, a relative of her father, …

genesis.29.p4.b4.text: … and she ran and told her father.

genesis.29.p5.b1.text: When Laban heard the news about his sister’s son Jacob, he ran out to meet him. He embraced him and kissed him …

genesis.29.p5.b2.text: … and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him all that had happened.

genesis.29.p5.b3.text: “You are indeed my own flesh and blood.”

genesis.29.p5.b4.text: After Jacob had stayed with him a month …

genesis.29.p6.b1.text: “Just because you are my relative, should you work for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be.”

genesis.29.p6.b2.text: Now Laban had two daughters; the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.

genesis.29.p6.b3.text: “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”

genesis.29.p6.b4.text: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.

genesis.29.p7.b1.text: “Grant me my wife, for my time is complete …”

genesis.29.p7.b2.text: So Laban invited all the men of that place and prepared a feast.

genesis.29.p7.b3.text: But when evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob, …

genesis.29.p7.b4.text: And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maidservant.

genesis.29.p8.b1.text: When morning came, there was Leah!

genesis.29.p8.b2.text: “What have you done to me?” … “Why have you deceived me?”

genesis.29.p8.b3.text: “It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older.”

genesis.29.p8.b4.text: … he loved Rachel more than Leah. So he worked for Laban another seven years.

genesis.29.p9.b1.text: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.

genesis.29.p9.b2.text: “The LORD has seen my affliction. Surely my husband will love me now.”

genesis.29.p9.b3.text: “Now at last my husband will become attached to me, because I have borne him three sons.”

genesis.29.p9.b4.text: “This time I will praise the LORD.”
